title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Construction-site clean-up
audience: Owners and account managers of construction-site clean-up businesses who quote regular site housekeeping and waste work for principal contractors and builders.
learningOutcomes: Write a site clean-up offer with a clear promised standard, visit frequency, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a principal contractor carries on site, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only on time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'We clean up building sites' is a service. 'We keep the amenities, walkways and waste areas to the site rules every working day, with a checklist signed in the site diary, bins collected to the agreed schedule, and a return within one working day for any item the site manager flags' is an offer. The principal contractor buys a site that meets its own rules and a supplier that will not need supervising.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome, such as a site kept to the principal contractor's housekeeping standard; a defined visit pattern that fits the trades' program; the work the principal contractor must do, such as providing the bin location, site induction and access; the certainty you provide, such as a daily checklist in the site diary; and the risk you carry, such as the return visit. Keep each part specific and checkable. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', last updated 1 August 2025). The principal contractor sets the site rules, so write the offer to fit them.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make the induction, the bin arrangement and the sign-off step simple. One named contact on site, one agreed bin and waste location, and one diary entry each day reduce the decisions the principal contractor has to make. Principal contractors often accept a higher price for a subcontractor that arrives on time, follows the site rules and needs no chasing, because the client pays for reliability on a busy site.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', last updated 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria explains that a service provider gets a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (last updated 13 October 2023), but that page sets no fix window, so write your own. Do not publish a measured claim, such as a percentage of site inspections passed, unless you can show the record. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: No pricing source for construction-site clean-up was found in the research, so this lesson does not give a site rate, a skip cost or a labour rate. The FairWorkMate pay rate in the research is for cleaning services, not the building and construction awards, so it must not be used as a site labour rate. Price from your own hours and cost (see BP-05 and HBM-12), then state the total and say whether GST is included (ACCC, last modified 15 July 2026). Skip hire and waste disposal are separate costs: quote them from your own supplier, and show them as separate lines on the quote (Business Queensland, last updated 16 November 2022). Stepped packages, such as a daily clean, a weekly deep clean and a waste-removal add-on, can show the principal contractor what each level adds (Jobber Academy, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024).

procedure: Write the clean-up outcome in one sentence the site manager would repeat.
Set a visit pattern that fits the trades' program, and record how often you meet it.
List what the principal contractor must do, such as the induction, the bin location and access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a daily checklist signed in the site diary.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can staff it within the time you state.
Price from your own hours and cost, separate the skip and waste lines, then check the total and the scope.

workedExamples.situation: A subcontractor is asked to quote a weekly clean-up for a $400,000 renovation. The principal contractor wants a fixed weekly price, and the site rules assign housekeeping to subcontractors. No price source was found for this work.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Write the offer and say what price basis you can support.
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer states the daily checklist, the diary sign-off, the bin location, the return-visit promise and the exclusions, such as skip hire and waste disposal unless they are quoted separately. The price is built from your own hours and cost. The research found the principal contractor's duties for a project of this size under the 2015 code (a project costing $250,000 or more needs a principal contractor and a written WHS management plan), so the offer must fit the site's plan. Illustrative figures only: 8 crew-hours a week plus a 10 per cent allowance is 8.8 hours, at a cost of $55 an hour (illustrative) that is $484, and a 25 per cent target margin on price gives $645.33 a week. Replace these with your own records before any quote is issued.

commonErrors.error: Making a return-visit promise you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the promise to a return visit within the time you can staff, and write the time into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as 'site always clean'
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the checklist standard you can show, and keep the diary records.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. Site rules, induction and principal contractor duties come from the principal contractor and from work health and safety law. The research read the $250,000 threshold and the written WHS management plan in the 2015 construction code (approved 17 December 2015). It read the general construction induction and waste duties only in the 2012 code text, which is historical, so confirm that wording in the 2015 instrument. Victoria has its own OHS Act and regulations, which were not checked. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority.

qualityStandard: Every site offer states the standard, visit pattern, client inputs, return-visit promise and GST status, and is checked against your own hours and cost. No unsourced rate is used.
documentationEvidence: Written site offer with scope, checklist, exclusions and visit pattern, the price basis, and the decision made.
summary: A site offer promises a checkable housekeeping standard, fits the principal contractor's site rules, and states its exclusions.
No site clean-up pricing source was found, so price from your own hours and cost, and keep skip and waste as separate lines.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a site offer does the principal contractor buy?
What should a return-visit promise be?

Only for new clients and friends
Something you can deliver and afford
